Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: The study contains two primary axes of comparison: 1) Disease status/grade (Biopsy-negative vs NAG-PCa vs AG-PCa) and 2) The effect of a clinical procedure (Pre-DRE vs Post-DRE). The DRE is treated as a perturbation here because the authors explicitly state it 'can significantly change the levels of specific proteins'. The Pre/Post DRE comparison is mapped to 'un-classified' as it is a procedural state rather than a standard chemical, genetic, or disease-state perturbation defined in the ontology.

search_parameters: The fixed modification was on carbamidomethylation of cysteine (C). The variable modifications were on oxidation of methionine (M) and acetylation of protein N-terminal.
Since N-glycosylated asparagine (N) is converted to aspartic acid (D) by PNGase F treatment, conversion of N to D was set as a variable modification as well.

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: The experiment focuses on N-linked glycosites. The critical processing step is the use of PNGase F, which necessitates the search for N->D conversion at the glycosylation sites.
